tagline.text: Quiet World Heritage rice terraces tucked into eastern Ifugao

location.label: Location
location.text: Mayoyao, Ifugao (about 63 km from Lagawe, east of Banaue)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,000–6,000 (estimate for 2 nights and 3 days from Manila, including transport, lodging, food and a guide)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Overland from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), Manila

children.text: Mayoyao is one of the five clusters of the Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras, inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1995, and it is far quieter than Banaue. It is a good place to enjoy rice terraces, waterfalls, wartime relics and traditional festivals at a relaxed pace.

Mayoyao is a mountain town in Ifugao province, in the Cordillera highlands of northern Luzon. According to Wikipedia, it covers about 238 km², sits at around 1,186 m above sea level, and its highest point reaches 2,122 m. It is about
63km
from the provincial capital, Lagawe, and about
414km
from Manila by road. The 2024 census counted about 15,500 residents, who speak Ifugao (Tuwali), Ilocano and Tagalog.

The terraces here form the Mayoyao Central cluster, one of five clusters in the UNESCO site "Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras," inscribed in 1995. The others are Batad and Bangaan (both in Banaue), Hungduan, and Nagacadan (in Kiangan). The property was on the List of World Heritage in Danger from 2001 to 2012 and was removed after conservation efforts were recognized. Above the terraces lies a communally managed private forest called the muyong, which supplies water. The way the forest, paddies and irrigation channels work as one cultural landscape was the basis for the listing.

Mayoyao's appeal is how few people come. Wikivoyage notes that these terraces are often overlooked by tourists, who mostly stay in nearby Banaue. Terraces cover more than half of the town's area, so layered paddies are in view almost everywhere. It suits travelers who find the crowded viewpoints of Banaue and Batad tiring and want a closer look at everyday Ifugao life. The area also has historical weight. From July 26 to August 9, 1945, the Battle of Mayoyao Ridge took place, in which Filipino guerrillas led by Donald Blackburn, supported by US Army Air Forces airstrikes, drove out the Japanese garrison. The victory led to General Tomoyuki Yamashita's surrender at Kiangan. A memorial marker stands on Mount Nagchajan, the battle site.

There is disagreement about how old the terraces are. UNESCO describes them as more than 2,000 years old, but recent research by the Ifugao Archaeological Project suggests they were built after Spanish contact, about 400 years ago, starting with taro and switching to rice around 1600. Either way, they are the result of centuries of building by hand and maintaining water channels. Today residents grow legumes, ginger and tomatoes alongside rice, and farming and tourism are the heart of the local economy. Wikipedia also points out that tourism has led some paddies to be turned into housing and lodging lots and some traditional houses to be sold, so it helps to use local businesses and guides so that your money stays with residents.

These terraces cover more than half of the town and are one of the five World Heritage clusters. The color of the paddies changes a lot between planting and harvest, so timing your trip adds to the experience. The paddy dikes are narrow and slippery, so it is best to walk them with a local guide.

This is one section of the Mayoyao terraces, reached from the village of Chaya. According to Ivan Henares's blog, Chaya is the starting point of a rice harvest experience tour (Pfoto' Ad Majawjaw), and part of the proceeds goes to a heritage trust fund that introduces Mayoyao's traditional culture to younger generations. Check with the Mayoyao tourism office whether it is currently running.

Mount Nagchajan in Chaya was a Japanese stronghold during the Battle of Mayoyao Ridge. Caves, foxholes and a small war memorial remain, and the views open wide. It pairs well with the terraces for anyone interested in history.

blocks.title: A'pfaw Mahencha Falls and Khohang Garden

children.text: This three-tiered waterfall in Chumang can be seen from the viewing deck of Khohang Garden, a mountainside garden with pine trees. The trail down to the falls has 536 steps, and you must climb back up, so pace yourself. The three-tiered Tenogtog Falls in Inwaloy is also a good stop during a trek, but the path is slippery just after the rains.

This peak of about 2,702 m sits on the boundary of Mayoyao, Banaue and Mountain Province, and on clear days the view is said to reach the Isabela plains. Hiking and climbing require permission from local authorities, so ask the Mayoyao tourism office in advance.

blocks.title: Traditional stone tombs and Lumaguid Stone

children.text: Balangbang and Banhal have traditional Ifugao stone tombs (apfo'or), and the Banhal one is behind Mayoyao Hostel. In Buninan, the large boulder called Lumaguid Stone sits by the Balangbang River, with a legend connected to the town's prosperity.

This cultural festival is held every year on the last Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of April, with traditional Ifugao songs and dances. On August 8–9, the Lenong Peace Festival commemorates the Battle of Mayoyao Ridge. Dates can change from year to year, so check the latest announcements.

According to Ivan Henares's blog, Mayoyao has a museum that demonstrates how a traditional Mayoyao house is built. No opening hours or admission details are known, so ask at the town tourism office before you go.
Start at the municipal tourism office in Mayoyao to arrange a terrace guide and village activities. The
Philippine Tourism Promotions Board guide
directs visitors to the office to arrange a stay in a traditional Ifugao house and agricultural activities.
Walk around the town viewpoint, the Banhal stone tombs and the market area, then watch the terraces at sunset from your lodging's viewpoint.
Walk the Chaya terraces and Mount Nagchajan with a guide. The paths are narrow, so start early.
Head back toward Banaue or Santiago City to match the bus schedule. Always confirm the last departure the day before.
Public transport to Mayoyao runs only a few times a day, so the timetable effectively sets your itinerary.
After arriving in Mayoyao, explore the town, a terrace viewpoint and the stone tombs.
Combine Khohang Garden and A'pfaw Mahencha Falls in Chumang with Tenogtog Falls in Inwaloy for a full day of trekking.
See Chaya and Mount Nagchajan, then move on. If your fitness and permits allow, it is better to schedule Mount Amuyao as a separate outing.
Book Manila to Banaue using the
official Coda Lines booking page
. A 2026 listing gives
one way across two coach classes. Check the terminal printed on your ticket.
Santiago City in Isabela is another gateway. A
Mayoyao visitor report
allows about
4–5 hours
by bus from Santiago terminal. Check the departure time of the connecting bus first.
Mayoyao is about
414km
from Manila by road, so traveling there and staying overnight is the realistic plan.
Bus times and fares change often. Check at the terminal or with the Mayoyao tourism office before you leave.
Buses and jeepneys between Mayoyao and Banaue, Lagawe, Santiago or Solano are infrequent. Check the Mayoyao connection even if your bus gets to Banaue early.
One source gives the distance from Banaue to Mayoyao as about
42km
, but the mountain road makes it a long trip.
The main arrival and return terminal in Mayoyao is near the public market. Ask locally about departures and market-day pickup points.
Tricycles operate in town. Wikivoyage advises that a 4WD or another vehicle suited to mountain roads is best, and that most attractions require long hikes.
Wikivoyage gives the hiking season as the dry season, November to May. Climate statistics on Wikipedia show annual rainfall of about
, with August the wettest month and April the driest.
The look of the paddies moves from the clear water of planting season to green growth to the gold of harvest. The exact timing varies each year, so confirm locally.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: A good time for trekking and photos. Mornings and evenings are chilly, so bring a jacket.
The Igkhumtad ad Majawjaw festival is held in late April. Watch out for sun on exposed slopes.
August is the wettest month. Beware of landslides and slippery ground. The Lenong Peace Festival takes place on August 8–9.

items.label: Entrance and environmental fees
items.note: Ask the tourism office which registration and environmental fees apply to your viewpoint or guided walk.

items.label: Guide fee
items.note: Ask the municipal tourism office about the route, per-group or per-person fees and transport.

items.label: Lodging
items.note: Ask Mayoyao Hostel in Banhal or Mayoyao View Inn in Poblacion directly. The tourism office coordinates traditional-house stays.

items.label: Meals
items.note: Eat at cafés and restaurants in town.

items.label: Coda Lines from Manila to Banaue
items.note: 2026 listing for 45- and 35-seat buses. The local leg to Mayoyao from Banaue or Santiago costs extra.

items.label: Tricycle
items.note: Used for short trips within town.

The lodgings listed on Wikivoyage are homestay-style places: Mayoyao Hostel and Viewpoint (Banhal), Mayoyao View Inn (Poblacion), Helen's Guest House (Lower Onagol) and Milcah Lodge (Poblacion). Prices are not published, so it is safest to ask by phone or message in advance. Ivan Henares's writing says his hostel overlooks the terraces.

Eating places listed include Maura's Cafe (Poblacion) and Café Carmen (Bato-Alatbang). Maura's Cafe is known for Japanese freshwater eel (pikaw) and pigeon pea soup. Pfajah, a local rice wine, is mentioned as the area's signature drink. Wikivoyage notes there are no banks or ATMs in town and that everything is paid in cash, so bring plenty of cash.
There are said to be no banks or ATMs in Mayoyao town, so withdraw cash in Banaue or Santiago City beforehand.
Buses are infrequent, so confirm the return departure time as soon as you arrive.
The paths are narrow and slippery, so bring shoes with good grip and a walking stick.
Tell the
Mayoyao tourism office
which terraces and walking route you want. Ask about booking a guide, entry and environmental fees, and hiking permits. The local directory lists mayoyaotourism02@gmail.com.
The paddies are farmers' livelihoods. Do not step on the dikes carelessly or touch the crops.
When taking photos, ask local people for permission first.
Mountain journeys are long, so motion-sickness medicine and a warm layer are useful.
On a short trip you can combine Banaue and Batad, but Mayoyao is most rewarding if you stay at least one night.
The public market is in Bato-Alatbang. Stock up on snacks, water and small change for cash payments there.
Landslides and accidents are common on the mountain roads, many stretches have low or no guardrails, and fog adds to the danger. Be sure to check your vehicle's condition.
Roads can be cut or delayed in the rainy season, so check current road conditions.
Terrace trekking is slippery. Do not walk alone; go with a guide.
It is cool at altitude, but watch for sun and exhaustion on exposed slopes.
No verified information on mobile coverage was found, so download offline maps.
Rules and fees in the heritage area can change, so check the latest announcements.
Ifugao's best-known rice terraces, reached west along the mountain road, and the gateway to Mayoyao.
Another UNESCO cluster, famous for its amphitheater shape, reached on foot.
Another cluster of the same World Heritage Site, good to visit together with the hot springs.
A town in Mountain Province known for its caves and hanging coffins, easy to combine with an Ifugao trip.
